hints.title: Prefix Path Sharing Obstacle
hints.text: Searching a list of words for prefixes takes time proportional to the number of words. How can words sharing common prefixes share common tree paths to make prefix lookups independent of dictionary size?

hints.title: Character Node Branching
hints.text: Each node in the tree represents a single character and branches into subsequent characters, with a marker indicating where complete words terminate.

hints.title: Prefix Tree Node Traversal Procedure
hints.text: Each node maintains a map of character to child node and a boolean flag is_end. To insert, traverse characters creating new nodes as needed, setting is_end on the last. To search, follow characters; return true if path exists and is_end is true. For startsWith, return true if the character path exists.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: L: length of query word or prefix (1 <= L <= 2000)
T: total characters across all inserted words
complexity.notes: All operations insert, search, and startsWith run in strictly O(L) time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking prefixes against a hash set of words requires scanning every word, taking O(N * L) time which is too slow for large word lists.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sharing common prefixes among words compresses prefix storage and guarantees O(L) time per query independent of total word count.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clear node representation (array of size 26 or dictionary), correct distinction between search (requires is_end) and startsWith (only requires prefix path), and constant-time per character transitions.
